```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source(here::here("Code", "00_setup.R"))
library(knitr)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
read_table <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_tables, file), encoding = "UTF-8")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
flow <- read_table("mortality_flow.csv")
alignment <- read_table("exposure_alignment.csv")

# Preliminary results quoted below, each from the table of its page
ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 2) {
  sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(estimate, digits), fmt(low, digits), fmt(high, digits))
}
lag_main <- get_param("models", "lag_main")
main_or <- read_table("models_main_or.csv")[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup == "all" &
                                              model == "compound" & lag == lag_main]
or_main <- function(term_value) main_or[term == term_value, ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
reoi_all <- read_table("models_main_interaction.csv")[measure == "REOI"]
reoi_all[, `:=`(estimate = as.numeric(estimate), low = as.numeric(low), high = as.numeric(high))]
reoi_main <- reoi_all[outcome == "non_accidental" & subgroup == "all" & lag == lag_main,
                      ci(estimate, low, high, 3)]
reoi_excluding_zero <- reoi_all[, sum(low > 0 | high < 0)]
adjusted <- read_table("sensitivity_adjustment_or.csv")[
  outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main & term == "e01"]
all_three <- paste(names(get_param("sensitivity", "adjustment_increments")), collapse = " + ")
ozone_adjusted <- adjusted[adjustment == all_three, ci(or, or_low, or_high)]
lags_or <- read_table("lags_compound_or.csv")[outcome == "non_accidental"]
later <- lags_or[lag %in% c("2", "3")]
lags_grid <- read_table("lags_grid.csv")[outcome == "non_accidental" & estimable == TRUE &
                                           lag == "cumulative" & adjustment == "none"]
stopifnot(nrow(lags_grid) == uniqueN(lags_grid[, .(heatwave, ozone)]))
burden <- read_table("burden_estimates.csv")[
  outcome == "non_accidental" & lag == lag_main & or_source == "age-specific" &
    level == "total" & category == "any"]
# Heatwave days of each municipality over the study period, working definition
heatwave_days <- read_table("series_annual_by_municipality.csv")[
  !is.na(com), .(days = sum(heatwave_days)), by = municipality][order(-days)]
```

## The study

Does a day that is both a heatwave day and a high-ozone day carry a risk of
death larger than the sum of the two separate risks? The study answers it for
the 33 urban municipalities of Santiago (Santiago Province plus Puente Alto)
in the warm seasons, 1 November to 31 March, of 2009 to 2020, with a
space-time-stratified case-crossover design and conditional logistic
regression.

Principal investigator: Estela Blanco, Pontificia Universidad Católica de
Chile. Data analysis: Amaru Agüero Jiménez. Funded by ANID FONDECYT 11240322.

## Data in one paragraph

Temperature comes from CR2MET v2.5 (daily maximum and minimum by municipality).
Ozone, PM2.5 and nitrogen dioxide come from the SINCA monitoring network,
interpolated to one point per municipality by inverse distance weighting and
ordinary kriging. Deaths come from the open records of the Department of Health
Statistics and Information (DEIS). The exposure dataset has
`r fmt(alignment$rows[1])` municipality-days; the mortality dataset has
`r fmt(flow[step == "Non-accidental cause (A00-R99)", deaths])` non-accidental
deaths.

## Findings of the data checks

These are the points a reader of the results should know before anything else.
Each is documented in the deliverable named.

1. **The reference heatwave script counts consecutive days across
   municipalities.** In `HeatWave_PretermBirth_Chile`, the lag that defines
   "consecutive days" runs over rows of a table with all municipalities
   stacked. This project counts them within each municipality.
   ([Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-quality-control))
2. **CR2MET has no 29 February.** The three leap days of the study period are
   filled by interpolation and flagged. ([Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-quality-control))
3. **The delivered ozone series understates the days with most ozone.** Its
   station inputs were trimmed at the 99th percentile of the hourly values,
   which removes the afternoon peaks of the hottest days.
   ([Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation))
4. **Part of the delivered ozone series rests on imputed station values.**
   Station-days without a validated measurement were filled by imputation; the
   Independencia monitor, which failed in 2016, has no validated record for
   most of that year. ([Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation))
5. **The plan names the daily maximum 8-hour mean (MDA8); the delivered series
   is a 24-hour mean.** The exposure dataset now holds three ozone series:
   delivered, 24-hour mean rebuilt from validated records, and MDA8.
   ([Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-ozone-validation))
6. **A fixed threshold of 30 °C is not comparable across municipalities**,
   because the CR2MET value of a municipality describes its whole territory,
   mountains included. ([Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-quality-control))
7. **The temperature of a municipality is not always that of the place where
   people live.** `r heatwave_days$municipality[1]` has the most heatwave days
   of the 33 (`r heatwave_days$days[1]` with the working definition, against
   `r min(heatwave_days$days)` to `r heatwave_days$days[2]` in the others): the
   CR2MET series describes the whole territory of the municipality, and its
   hot days come in longer spells.
   ([Deliverable 1](deliverable_1_exposure.html#sec-heatwave-municipalities))
8. **COVID-19 deaths fall outside non-accidental mortality as defined in the
   plan** (A00-R99). ([Deliverable 2](deliverable_2_mortality.html#sec-deaths))

## Preliminary results

With the working definitions, which the principal investigator has not
confirmed (heatwave `r get_param("models", "heatwave_main")`, ozone above the
`r get_param("models", "ozone_cutoff_main")`th percentile of the municipality
in the delivered series, lag `r lag_main`). They are not findings to cite.

1. **Odds of non-accidental death against days with neither exposure:**
   `r or_main("e10")` on heatwave-only days, `r or_main("e01")` on
   high-ozone-only days and `r or_main("e11")` on days with both.
   ([Deliverable 3](deliverable_3_models.html#sec-models))
2. **No additive interaction:** REOI `r reoi_main`. Across causes, age groups,
   sex and lags, `r reoi_excluding_zero` of the `r nrow(reoi_all)` intervals
   exclude zero, in both directions, about what chance alone gives.
   Adjustment and the choice of ozone series do not change it.
   ([Deliverables 3](deliverable_3_models.html#sec-interaction) and
   [4](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-sensitivity))
3. **The associations are on the day of exposure and the day after.** With
   the four lags in one model the odds ratios at lags 2 and 3 lie between
   `r fmt(min(later$or), 2)` and `r fmt(max(later$or), 2)`.
   ([Deliverable 4](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-lag-structure))
4. **Over the four days after exposure the picture is less clear.** With the
   four lags in one model the cumulative REOI is positive in
   `r lags_grid[estimate_reoi > 0, .N]` of the `r nrow(lags_grid)` combinations
   of heatwave definition and ozone cut-off, and its interval excludes zero in
   `r lags_grid[low_reoi > 0, .N]`, mostly with the 30 °C and EHF definitions.
   With the working definition it has the same sign and an interval that
   includes zero. Exploratory. ([Deliverable 4](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-lag-structure))
5. **The association with high ozone alone does not survive adjustment:**
   `r ozone_adjusted` with PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide and humidity in the model,
   and most of the association of ozone is shared with temperature.
   ([Deliverable 4](deliverable_4_sensitivity.html#sec-sensitivity))
6. **Attributable burden:** `r ci(burden$excess, burden$excess_low, burden$excess_high, 0)`
   excess deaths in the warm seasons of 2009 to 2020,
   `r fmt(burden$excess_pct_of_deaths, 1)`% of the non-accidental deaths, with
   unadjusted odds ratios. ([Deliverable 3](deliverable_3_models.html#sec-burden))

## Decisions pending

The pipeline runs on working values marked `TO CONFIRM` in
`config/config.yml`. Changing one of them and running `Code/run_all.R` rebuilds
everything.

| Decision | Working value | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| Season of the temperature percentiles | All days of the year | Warm season only |
| 29 February | Interpolated | Left missing |
| Temperature of the municipalities that reach into the Andes | The CR2MET series of the whole territory, as delivered | Temperature of the populated area from the CR2MET grid; models without the municipality as a sensitivity analysis |
| Ozone series of the main analysis | Delivered 24-hour mean (`o3`) | Rebuilt 24-hour mean (`o3obs`), MDA8 (`o3mda8`) |
| Status of the hourly records | Validated only | Also preliminary and not validated |
| Interpolation method of the main analysis | IDW | Ordinary kriging |
| Scope of the ozone percentiles | Within each municipality | Pooled |
| Kriging values below zero | Set to missing | Truncated at zero |
| Headline definitions of the models | Heatwave `hw_p95_2d`, ozone above the 75th percentile | Any cell of the grid |
| Primary lag | Lag 0 | Lag 1, or lags 0 to 3 together |
| Reference category | Every non-heatwave day at or below the ozone cut-off | Ozone at or below the 50th percentile, as worded in the plan |
| Temperature in the continuous models | Percentile within the municipality, warm season | Degrees Celsius |
| Age groups of the rates per 100,000 | 0-64 and 65 or more (INE gives one group for 80 or more) | Another population source for 65-84 and 85 or more |
| Months of the pandemic | Kept, COVID-19 deaths outside the outcome | Excluded |

## Reproducing the work

Two commands, from the project folder, run everything:

```
Rscript Code/run_all.R
python3 Code/run_python.py
```

The first is the R pipeline, which in RStudio is started with the Source button
on `Code/run_all.R`. It installs the R packages that are missing, checks the
inputs, runs the checks of the methods, the scripts in order and the R
reports, and then compares every table with its copy from before the run. The
second renders the reports written in Python, which compare their own results
with those of R; it prepares its Python packages by itself and is not needed
by the first. The whole project runs from its own folder: the scripts find it
through the RStudio project file, and no path of a particular computer appears
in the code. Three files make a run repeatable on another computer:

- `Data/input_manifest.csv` gives the size and checksum of every input file.
  Each script stops if an input is missing or is not the listed file. The
  inputs and their sources are described in `Data/README.md`; none of the data
  are in the repository.
- `Output/run_environment.txt` and `Output/run_environment_python.txt`
  describe the machine that last ran each of the two, which produced the
  tables of the repository: system, R, Quarto, Python and package versions.
- `renv.lock` and `requirements.txt` hold a complete set of package versions,
  those of the first machine on which the project was run. The two files above
  list where a machine differs from them.

The pipeline has been run from the inputs on two machines: Linux with R 4.3.3,
and macOS on Apple silicon with R 4.5.2 and the current packages. The results
of the main analysis agree between them within a relative difference of 2e-11.
The results built on the ordinary kriging that the project computes itself
(the rebuilt series `o3obs_ok` and `o3mda8_ok`, and the cross-validation) differ
from the third decimal of their odds ratios: on about one day in a hundred the
kriging system is close to singular and its solution changes with rounding in
the last digit, which the two machines do not do in the same way. Inverse
distance weighting, used for the main analysis, gives the same values on both.
On each machine a second run gives the tables of the first. The section
"Reproducibility" of the README of the repository has the details.
